prompt: A Sports Commerce & News Management System that includes offline sports content aggregation and a secure on-device shopping workflow for merchandise tied to teams and leagues. The app serves three roles: Administrator (configures ingestion sources, compliance settings, and audits), Editor/Analyst (reviews ingestion quality, investigates failures, and curates content), and Regular User (browses stories, manages cart, and views receipts). On the home screen, users can filter and search aggregated sports headlines, open article details, and save items for offline reading; a dedicated “Ingestion Console” lets Admins define RSS-like parsing and crawling rules, allow/block lists by domain/keyword, and an anti-scraping strategy based on randomized local user-agent rotation and per-source request pacing. Scheduled ingestion runs on device with configurable intervals (default every 6 hours), exponential backoff retries (3 attempts over 15 minutes), and a monitoring log that records source, rule version, items parsed, and failure reasons; repeated failures (5 in 24 hours) generate an in-app alert for Admin review. The cart experience supports add/remove/update quantities, guest-to-user cart merge at first login, real-time inventory validation against the locally stored catalog (prevent checkout if available quantity < requested), and a pricing engine with configurable rules such as 10% off orders over $50, one coupon per order, and tax calculated by stored state rate tables; a price-lock holds item prices for 30 minutes once checkout starts, after which the user must reconfirm. Online-only functions from upstream (WeChat login/real-name verification, SMS/email sending, webhooks, online payments/refunds) are explicitly out of scope; instead, the app provides in-app notifications only, with templates, variables (e.g., {orderId}, {total}), send logs, and retry for failed local deliveries. Data is persisted entirely on-device using Room (SQLite), with dependency injection via Koin and an Android Views UI; business logic is organized into ViewModel/UseCase layers with all IO and pricing computations off the main thread to prevent ANRs. Core data models include SourceRule, IngestionJobRun, Article, CatalogItem, InventorySnapshot, Cart, CartLineItem, PriceRule, Coupon, Notification, AuditEvent, DataBatchVersion, and DataLineage records; batches and versions track ingestion runs end-to-end, including rule version, timestamps, and lineage pointers from source to article. Rule-based quality validation runs after each batch (type/range/consistency checks, e.g., publish time must be within the last 365 days, price must be $0.01–$9,999.99, and inventory cannot be negative), producing quality metrics and in-app alerts when error rate exceeds 2% per batch. Security is enforced with local username/password login, salted password hashing, step-up re-authentication for exports and backup/restore, strict input validation to reduce injection-style payloads, and comprehensive audit logs for logins, authorization changes, edits, and exports. Sensitive fields (password hashes, any stored IDs) are masked in UI and logs, and encrypted at rest using Android Keystore-backed encryption; backups are local-only (user-initiated to device storage), with restore requiring confirmation and integrity checks. Performance targets include 60fps list scrolling using RecyclerView + DiffUtil, image downsampling with an LRU cache to keep peak image memory under 20MB, and indexed Room queries (composite indexes on sourceId+publishedAt, cartId+sku) designed to keep common searches under 50ms for up to 100,000 articles. The app complies with Android 10+ scoped storage and background restrictions, and scheduled work uses WorkManager constrained to run when the device is idle or charging to balance reliability and battery life.
